import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import least_squares
sst=np.sum((sigma-sigma.mean())**2)
rng=np.random.default_rng(2)
models={
 'E': lambda p: p[0]*np.sqrt(T)+p[1]*np.log(1+p[2]*eps)*T**2+p[3]*np.log(eps)+p[4]*np.exp(-p[5]*eps)*T**p[6],
 'G': lambda p: p[0]*np.sqrt(T)+p[1]*np.log(1+p[2]*eps)*T**2+p[3]*np.log(eps)*T**p[4]+p[5]*np.exp(-p[6]*eps)*np.exp(-p[7]/T),
 'H': lambda p: p[0]*np.sqrt(T)+p[1]*np.log(1+p[2]*eps)*T**2+p[3]*eps*np.exp(-p[4]*eps)*T**p[5]+p[6]*np.log(eps)*np.exp(-p[7]/T),
}
lo=np.full(9,-np.inf); hi=np.full(9,np.inf); lo[2]=1e-3; hi[2]=50
for name,f in models.items():
    best=(np.inf,None)
    for s in range(40):
        p0=rng.normal(0,1,9); p0[2]=rng.uniform(0.05,3)
        p0=np.clip(p0,lo+1e-6,hi-1e-6)
        try:
            r=least_squares(lambda p: np.nan_to_num(f(p)-sigma,nan=1e6), p0, bounds=(lo,hi), max_nfev=200)
            v=np.sum(r.fun**2)/sst
            if v<best[0]: best=(v,r.x)
        except Exception: pass
    print(name, best[0], np.round(best[1],5).tolist())
